findings.title: Arena Floor Texture Ambiguity
findings.problem: The floor texture is a low-contrast, repeating beige grid that looks identical to the 'Road' and 'City' textures. It lacks unique visual markers or distinct lighting.
findings.why: Players cannot distinguish the practice arena from the open world or highway at a glance. This creates confusion about the game mode and makes the environment feel like a placeholder rather than a dedicated combat zone.
findings.fix: Apply a distinct color tint (e.g., industrial grey or rust orange) to the arena floor and add high-contrast hazard striping or boundary lines to visually separate it from the travel maps.

findings.title: Radar Lack of Feedback
findings.problem: The radar is a static dark circle with a faint green sweep but no visible blips, targets, or environmental contours.
findings.why: It reads as broken or decorative rather than functional. In a survival game, the lack of immediate feedback on what is around you increases anxiety without providing tactical value, making the UI feel unfinished.
findings.fix: Even in empty zones, render a faint outline of the map boundaries or obstacles on the radar. When enemies appear, ensure they register as bright white/green dots immediately.

findings.title: HUD Text Legibility on Road
findings.problem: The top-center text box ('En route to Albany...') uses white text against a semi-transparent black background that sits directly over the moving asphalt texture.
findings.why: The contrast is insufficient when the car moves quickly; the eye struggles to separate the text from the road texture behind it. The transparency allows the noise of the road to bleed into the text area.
findings.fix: Increase the opacity of the text background box to near-solid black, or add a hard drop shadow/outline to the font to ensure it pops off the road surface.

findings.title: Vehicle Constructor Visual Disconnect
findings.problem: The vehicle preview is a flat, glowing blue wireframe, while the rest of the game uses textured pixel art.
findings.why: This breaks immersion and fails to communicate the actual look of the car being built. Players cannot see how their choices will affect the aesthetic of the vehicle in-game.
findings.fix: Render the preview using the same textured assets used in gameplay, perhaps with a slightly desaturated filter to indicate 'unfinalized' state, so players can see the car's colors and shape accurately.

findings.title: City Map Interaction Indicators
findings.problem: The interactive buildings and gates are small, grey squares that blend into the cracked pavement. Only the yellow chevrons provide some contrast.
findings.why: In a dense hub area, it is difficult to identify which structures are interactable versus just scenery. Players may miss objectives or get lost trying to find valid entry points.
findings.fix: Add a subtle glow or brighter border to the base of interactive buildings, and increase the brightness/saturation of the directional arrows so they stand out clearly against the grey ground.
